strategy_title: Autotuning num_warps/num_stages Without Tile Size Changes Regresses
strategy_description: Adding @triton.autotune that only varies num_warps and num_stages—without changing BLOCK_M, BLOCK_N, or BLOCK_K—caused registers per thread to jump from 128 to 255, halving achieved occupancy from 6.25% to 3.12% and increasing kernel duration by 42%. The autotune overhead and the compiler's register allocation for additional software-pipeline stages outweighed any latency-hiding benefit when tile sizes remained fixed at their original large values. When a kernel is already register-bound (128 regs/thread, occupancy limited by registers), adding num_stages without simultaneously reducing tile sizes will increase register pressure further and worsen occupancy.
slow_pseudocode:
# Before: fixed large tiles, no autotune
@triton.jit
def kernel(...):
    BLOCK_M: tl.constexpr = 64
    BLOCK_N: tl.constexpr = 64
    BLOCK_K: tl.constexpr = 64
    # 128 regs/thread, 6.25% occupancy
    ...
applicable_when: Never: this specific pattern (autotune only num_warps/num_stages with fixed large tile sizes on a register-bound kernel) is always harmful.
do_not_apply_when: Kernel is already register-bound (registers_per_thread >= 64, theoretical occupancy <= 25%); increasing num_stages without reducing BLOCK_M/BLOCK_N/BLOCK_K will increase register pressure and reduce occupancy further. Always pair num_stages increases with tile size reductions when register pressure is the occupancy limiter.
framework_notes: Triton: num_stages controls software pipelining depth and directly increases register usage for prefetch buffers. When BLOCK_K is large (e.g. 64), each additional pipeline stage allocates BLOCK_M*BLOCK_K or BLOCK_K*BLOCK_N additional registers for the prefetched tiles. The correct fix for a register-bound GEMM kernel is to reduce BLOCK_M, BLOCK_N, BLOCK_K in the autotune configs, not just vary num_warps/num_stages.
